text:
devon: Heads-up — after the routing change canary today I'm seeing tail-latency spikes on multi-model routes. Profiler points at a lot of small batches + KV cache misses. Anyone else seeing this?

marta: Yep. Dedicated-cluster-A trending up. Batch sizes dropped from ~6 -> ~2 on mixed-variant routes.

samir: Uploaded a quick profile dump: batch_formation: avg_size=2.1, pct95=4; kv_hits=72%, kv_miss=28% (previously ~92/8). CPU kernel time looks similar but end-to-end token latency up.

liz: Hypothesis: fallback/compat expansion is fragmenting queues — more variant diversity per queue -> small batches + more cold KV entries. Also noticed token_budget cap was lowered to 64 in the rollout.

devon: Trace link: https://perf.redwood/internal/trace/185555 (flame graph + batch trace). Kernel-selection logs show a few variants falling back to slower kernels for short seqs.

marta: Two quick mitigations: 1) increase queue headroom / allow slot merging for multi-variant queues, or 2) bias routing to be more sticky (prefer same variant) to keep batchability. Which is lower risk?

samir: I can run a microbench with toggles. Command I'll run: 
```
bench/run --workload=mix-3models --token_budget=64/128 --sticky_routing=true/false --samples=1000
```
Will post numbers in ~30m.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: rolled canary routing-v2 -> 20% at 2026-03-15T10:12:00 UTC

liz: Also saw KV warmup climb; cold entries appear after routing fans out to fallbacks. Suggest prefetching likely variant KV entries when a fallback is chosen (cheap heuristics).

devon: :eyes: Also want kernel-selection traces — if variants trigger less-optimal kernels for short sequences we compound latency even with same batch size.

marta: Inline perf snapshot I grabbed: baseline p95=120ms, canary p95=210ms; batch_avg_size baseline=5.6, canary=2.3; kv_hit baseline=91%, canary=69%.

samir: Running bench now. If the theory holds, increasing token_budget and enabling sticky should raise avg_batch and improve kv_hit. I'll test both together and separately.

liz: Note: sticky routing as mitigation could change quality for clients (they may not see fallbacks they expect). Need A/B eval on prompt set for any sticky rollout.

devon: Agree. Samir -> post perf + raw logs. Marta -> can you prepare a short rollout plan for a conservative canary?

marta: On it. Will add dashboard cards (p95, avg_batch_size, kv_hit, kernel_mismatch_rate) and alert thresholds. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: alert: dedicated-cluster-A p95 > 180ms at 2026-03-15T10:21:42 UTC

samir: Bench results: token_budget=64 + sticky=false => p95=208ms, avg_batch=2.4, kv_hit=70%
 token_budget=128 + sticky=true => p95=125ms, avg_batch=4.8, kv_hit=88% (kv hit improved after warmup). Posting raw logs to perf bucket.

devon: Nice numbers. Let's run sticky canary with token_budget=128 and watch for quality regressions. Samir/Liz — coordinate on eval set.

marta: Canary plan posted: 10% traffic, 1hr, auto-rollback if p95 > 150ms OR kv_hit < 80%. Dashboard links in the plan.

devon: I'll file a perf ticket to capture follow-up: compat-grouping heuristics, kernel-selection trace anomaly, and possible prefetch optimization. Reference this thread.

marta: Thanks all — will start canary and monitor.

samir: Logs/benchmarks uploaded: s3://perf-exports/185555-routing-bench.tar.gz

devon: Closing loop later today after canary window. Good troubleshooting + quick bench, appreciated.
